transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, but... I guess what brings me in is just some trouble I've been having with my eating. 

It's probably just a bad habit I need to break, not the worst thing in the world, but... well, after my late shifts, I'll usually stop for takeout on the way back. And I end up getting, you know, a pretty big meal—like two burgers, fries, a shake. Which I know is a lot for a guy my age, just trying to unwind. 

But the part that's sort of embarrassing is... I'll still go home and kind of keep going. I'll head out and clean out whatever leftovers we have in the garage fridge. It's almost like I'm having a whole second supper right after I just ate. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that sounds a bit silly, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
How often do you find yourself eating this extra amount of food after your initial takeout meal?

Well, um, it's not every single night, I promise. I really do try to keep it under control. But... I guess for the past few months, there's usually at least one night a week where I end up doing it. 

And, well, if I've had a really rough day on the line, or just a string of those late shifts, it might happen, you know, maybe two or three times a week? I hope that's not too terrible... does that give you the right idea of what's going on? I just don't want you to think I'm doing this all the time.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during those times when you have the extra food after the takeout meal?

Well, um... I mean, I try to be. I really do. It's not like I completely lose my mind or anything, I'm fully aware of what's happening. 

But... honestly? Once I start, it kind of feels like a switch is flipped. It's really embarrassing to admit, but even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Roy, just shut the bag and go inside,' it's like... well, my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. 

I know a grown man should have better willpower than that, and I'm really trying to do better. I hope you don't think less of me for it... does that make sense, how I'm describing it?
How do you feel after you've finished eating that extra food?

Well, um... I try not to beat myself up too much about it, because, you know, at the end of the day it's just food. But... honestly? I feel pretty ashamed. And, well, kind of disgusted with myself, if I'm being completely honest. 

I've just... I've always prided myself on being a dependable guy, you know? Disciplined. You kind of have to be in my line of work. So when I do this, it makes me feel like I'm... I don't know, sneaking around in my own house. Like I'm really letting myself down. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too pathetic for a guy my age. Am I explaining that okay for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you start with the extra food?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm completely unable to stop. I mean, I could stop if there was an emergency or something, I'm sure of it. 

But... yeah, like I was saying before, once I get going with that extra food, it's just... it's really hard to put the brakes on. I tell myself to stop, but it's like my body isn't listening to my brain. I don't want to make it sound like I'm totally out of control, because I'm really trying to work on it. 

I hope that answers your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information without sounding like I've completely lost the plot.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating the extra food?

Well, yeah... um, I guess it goes back to what I was saying just a minute ago. I really try not to let it get to me too much, but... yes, the guilt is definitely there. 

Like I mentioned, I just end up feeling so ashamed and, well, disgusted with myself. I've always prided myself on being a disciplined guy—being dependable is a really big deal to me. So doing this... it just makes me feel like I'm sneaking around and letting myself down. 

I hate to sound like a broken record about it, and I really am trying to be more positive and do better... but yeah, I do feel guilty. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much for you? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking.
Do you feel like you're eating really quickly when you have that extra food after the takeout meal?

Well, um... I guess I do eat it pretty fast. I mean, I'm usually out in my truck or, you know, tucked away in the workshop out back. 

I don't want to make it sound like I'm just shoveling it in or anything, but... yeah, I guess I eat it so fast that half the time I barely even taste it. It's almost like... like I'm just trying to get it down before somebody catches me, you know? Which is silly, because I'm a grown man, but... that's just how it feels. 

I try to slow down and chew my food properly, I really do. But in those moments, it just sort of... happens quickly. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right for you.
Do you feel like you're able to pause or stop eating once you've started with the extra food?

Well, um... I know we just touched on this a bit, and I really don't want to sound like I'm completely out of control, because I'm not... but, well, pausing is really tough. 

It's like... once I start, it feels like a switch just gets flipped. I'll be sitting there, literally telling myself, "Roy, shut the bag and go inside," but... my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. I know I should be able to just stop, and I'm really working on having more willpower, I promise. It's just... in that specific moment, it's a lot harder than it sounds. 

I hope that's the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture without making it sound worse than it is.
Do you feel like you're eating the extra food without really thinking about it?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm completely checked out or anything. I mean, I know I'm eating, obviously. 

It's not like I just black out and suddenly the food is gone. I'm aware of what I'm doing, I just... I guess I'm maybe not focusing on it as much as I should be? Like I said, I'm usually just trying to get it done quickly, so maybe I'm not really savoring every bite or thinking too deeply about it. But I'm definitely still present, you know? 

I really try to be mindful of what I'm doing, I do. I hope that answers your question? I'm not entirely sure if that's what you meant by "without thinking about it," but I hope it helps.
Do you usually eat the extra food when you're feeling stressed or upset?

Well, um... I guess stress could have a little something to do with it, maybe? 

I mean, I don't want to make excuses or sound like I'm blaming a tough day at work for my own choices. I'm pretty good at handling stress, usually. It's just... sometimes, after a really long shift on the floor, or if things get a bit tense around the house, I guess I might reach for that extra food a little more often. 

It's not like I'm crying into a burger or anything dramatic like that. It's just... maybe a way to unwind for a minute? I try not to let things get to me, I really do. I hope I'm not making it sound like I can't handle my own life, because I definitely can. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer here.
Do you think eating the extra food helps you feel better when you're stressed or upset?

Well, um... I guess maybe for a second it does? 

I really don't want to sound like I'm using food as a crutch, because I know that's not a healthy way to deal with things. I'm usually pretty good at just brushing off a bad day. But... yeah, I suppose in that exact moment, while I'm eating it, there's a little bit of relief, maybe? Just a quick distraction from whatever was bothering me. 

It doesn't last long, though, and I know I shouldn't rely on it. I'm really trying to find better ways to decompress, like maybe taking a walk or something. I hope that doesn't make me sound too weak or anything? I'm just trying to be honest about how it feels in the moment, if that's what you're asking.
How many times a month would you say you have one of these episodes where you eat the extra food after the takeout meal?

Well, um... if we're looking at a whole month, I guess it might add up a little bit? I really try to keep it under control, I promise I do. I don't want you to think I'm just doing this every single day. 

But... um, for the past few months, I'd say there’s usually at least one night a week where I end up doing this. And... well, sometimes, if I've had a really rough day on the line or a late shift at the plant, it might creep up to two or three times a week. So I guess that would be maybe eight to ten times a month, roughly? 

I hope that doesn't sound too awful. I know I need to be doing better with it, and I really am trying to cut back. I just want to be honest with you so we can fix it. Is that... does that give you the information you needed?
Do you feel like you have no control over your eating during these episodes?

Well, um... I guess "no control" sounds a little extreme, maybe? I mean, I'm a grown man, I should be able to just stop eating when I'm full, right? I really don't want to sound like I'm completely helpless or anything like that. 

But... well, I suppose once I actually start on that extra food, it kind of feels like a switch gets flipped somewhere. It's embarrassing to admit, but even while I'm sitting there in the car, literally telling myself, "Roy, just shut the bag and go inside," my hands just... they just keep reaching for more. It's like my brain knows I should stop, but I just can't seem to make myself do it in that moment. 

I know I need to be stronger than that, and I'm really going to work on it. I hope it doesn't make me sound too pathetic, admitting that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture so you can help me figure this out.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself from eating once you start with the extra food?

Well, um... I know we just kind of touched on this, and I really don't want to repeat myself too much and waste your time. But... yeah, I guess that's exactly it. 

I mean, I really try to be disciplined. I work hard all day, I follow the rules at the plant, so you'd think I could just put the brakes on with a bag of food, right? I really want you to know I'm not usually someone who just gives up. 

But... um, yeah, like I was saying, once I take that first bite of the extra stuff in the car, it's like that switch just flips. I'm literally sitting there, in my own head, saying, "Roy, you're done, just roll up the bag, grab your keys, and go inside the house." But my hands... they just keep going back into the bag. It's like I can't physically make myself stop until it's all gone. 

It sounds so silly when I say it out loud, and I'm really sorry if that makes me sound weak. I know I should be able to just stop. Does that... does that answer what you were asking about not being able to stop? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you usually eat the extra food when you're feeling anxious or upset, rather than just stressed?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't say I'm really an anxious person, or... or getting overly upset about things. I try to keep a pretty level head, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting in my car crying or having a panic attack or anything like that. I'm usually pretty steady.

It's mostly just... well, just the regular stress from the plant, like I mentioned. Long hours, being on my feet, trying to meet the quotas on the line. By the time I get off, I'm just... drained, I guess. So I wouldn't say it's because I'm upset or anxious. It's just a way to unwind after a hard shift. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I really am trying to be helpful.
Do you think eating the extra food is a way for you to deal with your emotions after a long day?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't really call it dealing with my emotions, exactly. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm, you know, eating my feelings or anything like that. That sounds a little... well, maybe a little too dramatic for a guy like me. 

I really try to handle my own problems and not let things get to me too much. It's more just... it's just a habit I've gotten into, I think. Just something to do when I finally sit down after being on the line for ten hours. It's not like I'm sitting there feeling super sad or angry and trying to cover it up with food. I just... I just want to relax for a minute before I go inside and start the whole evening routine.

I hope I'm not being difficult by saying that. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea of what's going on. Does that sound like what you were asking?
Do you usually feel guilty after eating the extra food?

Well, um... I guess... yeah, I do. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything, but... yeah, guilt is definitely part of it. 

I just... I've always prided myself on being dependable, you know? The guy who shows up, does the hard work, keeps everything on track. I really try to be a disciplined person. So when I sit there and eat all that extra food... well, afterward, I just feel... ashamed, I guess. Kind of disgusted with myself, if I'm being honest. 

It makes me feel like I'm sneaking around, like I'm doing something wrong and just letting myself down. I really hope you don't think less of me for admitting that. I know a grown man shouldn't be sneaking food in his car. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit.
How often do you have these episodes of eating extra food after a takeout meal in a typical month?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, for the past few months or so, it's been... well, usually at least one night a week. Sometimes, if it's been a really rough week on the line or a string of late shifts, it might be two or three times. 

I don't want it to sound like it's every single day or that it's completely out of control, you know? Most nights I just come straight home and have dinner with the family like a normal guy. It's just those particularly draining shifts where I end up slipping up a bit more. 

I hope that's not too terrible... I mean, I know it's not ideal, but I am trying to keep it in check. Does that frequency make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact details you need to help me out.
